headline: Democrats now hold both the House and the Senate, bitcoin is back near $78,000 after its election dip, and a French bank is named in a $133M crypto theft.

stories.title: Democrats win the House as well as the Senate; a top crypto critic returns
stories.summary: The AP called the House for Democrats early Wednesday, after calling the Senate late Tuesday when Iowa came in. Sherrod Brown won back an Ohio Senate seat despite heavy crypto industry spending against him.
points: The AP called the House for Democrats early on 4 Nov, after calling Senate control late Tuesday following Iowa, per Forbes.
Sherrod Brown beat Senator Jon Husted in Ohio; crypto groups Fairshake and Digital Freedom Fund spent about $63M against him, per CoinDesk.
Elizabeth Warren is positioned to lead the Senate Banking Committee, and Brown could get a senior role on the Agriculture Committee, which oversees the CFTC, per CoinDesk.
Saxo says a Democratic Senate from January "changes the arithmetic" for the CLARITY Act market-structure bill, stalled since September.
The CLARITY Act stalled after the Senate rejected a key procedural vote 49-50 in September, per AMBCrypto.

stories.title: Bitcoin recovers from its election dip, but money keeps leaving bitcoin ETFs
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell below $76,000 as the results came in, then bounced back above $78,000 once the outcome was clear. DeFi tokens led the rebound. US spot bitcoin funds are still seeing outflows and sentiment gauges still read fear.
points: Bitcoin fell to about $75,600 and then recovered to about $78,300, per CoinDesk.
CoinDesk's DeFi Select Index rose about 5% and ether about 2%, while TRUMP fell 7.1% and WLFI 5%; liquidations reached $469M, per CoinDesk.
US spot bitcoin ETFs had a net outflow of $115.56M on 3 Nov, the third day in a row, led by BlackRock's IBIT at -$94.98M, per TokenPost citing SoSoValue.
Spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $515M in October and about the same again in the first two trading days of November, per CoinDesk citing SoSoValue.

stories.title: A French bank is named in a $133M crypto theft, the latest in a run of hacks
stories.summary: Onchain investigator ZachXBT named Crédit Mutuel Arkéa as the suspected victim of a theft of more than $133M, with funds pulled out through big exchanges and laundered. It follows the Binance heist and the Mercado Bitcoin hack, keeping security at the top of users' worries.
points: ZachXBT first flagged more than $106M on 1-2 Nov, then found about $27M more, for over $133M, per CoinDesk.
Bitquery traced $108.8M in USDC withdrawn from Kraken, Crypto.com and OKX over 21 hours, per CoinDesk.
Sources differ on whether the bank has confirmed: CoinDesk reports it confirmed "an attack" with no financial consequences for clients; Decrypt says it has not publicly confirmed any theft.
More than $30M was laundered, partly through Monero, per Decrypt; ZachXBT has "high confidence" North Korea's Lazarus Group was not behind it, per CoinDesk.
Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin says it lost about $38M and will cover all customer losses; about $11M has been frozen, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Circle reports Q3 results
briefs.summary: Circle reported Q3 revenue of $865M, up 17% from a year earlier, with $73.9B of USDC in circulation at quarter-end; Binance is making a $100M equity investment, per Circle's release.

briefs.title: Hut 8 Q3: lower revenue, big paper gains
briefs.summary: Hut 8's revenue fell to $71.1M from $83.5M, while net income of $189.5M included $413.8M of mostly unrealized digital-asset gains; its buyback was raised to $1.0B, per the company.

briefs.title: CFTC sued over stock perps
briefs.summary: The Capital Markets Alliance, backed by Cboe and Citadel Securities, sued the CFTC in New York federal court, arguing single-stock perpetual futures belong under the SEC, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Treasury refunding due today
briefs.summary: The US Treasury's quarterly refunding statement is due at 13:30 GMT (8:30am ET, 20:30 Bangkok) today, per Saxo.

briefs.title: Miner stocks jump before earnings
briefs.summary: Riot and Cipher each rose more than 18% on Tuesday ahead of earnings; Riot holds its Q3 call today, per Saxo.
